match_note: Round 1 had R1, R2, R3; round 2 had R2, R3 and a new R4 (who adjudicated R1's charge-transfer and spin-orientation points; R2 and R4 raised no new issues). The reviewed manuscript carried a new title ('Evidence of competing ground states between fractional Chern insulator and antiferromagnetism in moire MoTe2' versus v1's 'Emergent charge-transfer ferromagnetism and Fractional Chern states in moire MoTe2') and R3 cites a July 2025 arXiv paper, so it was submitted after v1 (March 2025). But the referees' page/line references and specifics match v1: the 'never been observed in moire systems and any other material systems' sentence on page 4, the typos 'inplane'/'our-of-plane'/'Honeycomb', capitalized 'Magnetic' in the Fig. 1 caption, Fig. 1d-f/g-i layout, Fig. 1b never cited, RC and Tw used before definition, 'superlattice symmetry transition', ED Fig. 7e Rxx(T), ED Fig. 12 schematic. The Supplementary Information is not included in the v1 PDF, so SI-only items (SI section 1 errata) are marked in_v1 false. L2 concerns abstract wording added in revision.

concerns.quote: From both abstract and introduction, it is unclear what the new things this work brought to the community.
concerns.summary: The abstract and introduction do not say what this work adds to the heavily studied tMoTe2 field.

concerns.quote: the authors for a few times stressed the “unexpected” AFM states. Why is it unexpected? I felt the field of study has reported such magnetic states many times
concerns.summary: Calling the AFM state unexpected is questioned because AFM-like states have been reported in other twisted systems.

concerns.quote: The claim here about the first pure electric field control of an AFM-FM transition may be true, but the result is similar in spirit to that of (Huang... bilayer CrI3
concerns.summary: The claim of a first pure electric-field-driven AFM-FM transition overlooks bilayer CrI3 electrical control (R2) and the field-induced insulator to QAH transition in MoTe2/WSe2 (R3).

concerns.quote: The authors suggest “charge transfer” as the mechanism. What are the charge transfer coming from? It is transferred from metal electrode to the tMoTe2, or self doping
concerns.summary: The proposed charge-transfer mechanism does not say where the transferred charge comes from (contacts or interlayer redistribution).

concerns.quote: Why is it not because of electric field effect? ... They should do this experiment and analysis.
concerns.summary: The effect could come from the electric field itself rather than doping; the authors should separate field and doping with the two gates (R1), and say which one is being tuned (R2).

concerns.quote: The authors thought if it is in-plane, the MCD should keep constant while B field is applied out of plane, which is not true.
concerns.summary: The argument used to rule out in-plane magnetization is flawed: an out-of-plane field could gradually raise the MCD or cause a spin flop.

concerns.quote: I’m wondering whether the same applies for an in-plane 120 antiferromagnet with strong Ising SOC
concerns.summary: The plateau in magnetization and finite-temperature susceptibility peak may not distinguish the proposed out-of-plane VP-AFM from an in-plane 120-degree IVC-AFM.

concerns.quote: until reading the SI section 7, it is not clear that the authors propose that the AFM state has out-of-plane spins (it is VP-AFM)
concerns.summary: The main text does not make clear that the proposed AFM has out-of-plane spins, a new state distinct from the better understood IVC-AFM.

concerns.quote: What do the authors attribute these different phase diagrams to? Is there any clear difference in the samples, e.g.: what is the distance to the gates in each device?
concerns.summary: A nanoSQUID study finds VP-FM at filling 1 for all angles 2.1 to 3.7 degrees, so sample differences (gate distance, disorder) may explain the AFM; disorder should be estimated.

concerns.quote: at smaller and larger angles, the strongest VP-FM occurs at E=0, following the exchange mechanism. Is there any reason why intermediate angles are special?
concerns.summary: Why the charge-transfer ferromagnetism appears only at intermediate twist angles is not explained.

concerns.quote: clarify which type of AFM is predicted by the theory outside the VP-FM region; is it an IVC-AFM? ... Are there any parameters in the phase diagram where the VP-AFM is the ground state?
concerns.summary: The theory section should say which AFM it predicts and whether a VP-AFM ground state exists anywhere in the model, since this bears on the charge-transfer mechanism.

concerns.quote: Is it possible to determine whether the reemergent VP-FM state at the smallest twist angle is topological or trivial?
concerns.summary: Whether the VP-FM at the smallest twist angle is a Chern insulator or a trivial ferromagnet is not determined.

concerns.quote: I was wondering whether it is possible to locate the (split) van Hove line in the density-displacement field diagram
concerns.summary: The van Hove line could be located to see whether it coincides with fillings where VP-FM disappears.

concerns.quote: whether the measured Rxx could also be compatible with the scenario proposed in Ref. [10.1103/PhysRevX.12.021064], where Rxx decreases due to the appearance of an in-gap quasiparticle peak
concerns.summary: The non-monotonic Rxx versus T could come from an in-gap quasiparticle peak killed by magnetic order, not the authors' fluctuation-freezing picture.

concerns.quote: In the hall resistivity data at v=1 filling, there still seems to be an appreciable plateau at 4K which seems to be missing from the MCD data.
concerns.summary: Transport and MCD disagree at 4 K at filling 1: a Hall plateau persists that the MCD does not show.

concerns.quote: the size and shape of the antiferromagnetic region in panel e is of a very similar size and shape as that of the ferromagnetic region in panel f
concerns.summary: The AFM region in Fig. 1e resembles the FM regions in Fig. 1f and Fig. 2a; is there a common mechanism?

concerns.quote: The manuscript is lacking in many details and definitions that renders it unintelligible for any reader who is not already extremely knowledgeable about tMoTe2.
concerns.summary: Heavy acronym use and missing definitions and labels make the paper hard to follow for non-specialists.

concerns.quote: The readability of most figures is still low. ... It is good to add brief legends to indicate the different conditions
concerns.summary: Figure panels with identical legends but different curves need legends stating the measurement conditions.

concerns.quote: Multiple typos need to be fixed. “inplane” is not a word
concerns.summary: Several typos and capitalization errors need fixing.

concerns.quote: In summary paragraph, please explain in a more clear manner what are the major finding and proved mechanism, instead of only simply re-stating the experimental observation.
concerns.summary: The summary restates observations instead of stating the main findings and mechanism.

concerns.quote: the authors have not defined what ν_h is.
concerns.summary: The hole filling factor symbol is not defined.

concerns.quote: The manuscript never references Figure 1b
concerns.summary: Fig. 1b is never referenced in the text.

concerns.quote: The manuscript has not defined RC
concerns.summary: Reflectance contrast (RC) is used in the main text before it is defined.

concerns.quote: While the authors define Tw in the caption of ED fig. 9 and on page 7 they do not define it before its use here
concerns.summary: The Weiss temperature Tw is used before it is defined.

concerns.quote: It would be very helpful for readers to label the filling factor on the panels of Figs. 2 b-e
concerns.summary: Fig. 2b-e panels should be labelled with filling factor.

concerns.quote: The authors have left out the MCD subscript on chi
concerns.summary: The MCD subscript is missing on the susceptibility symbol.

concerns.quote: Panels d-e have no units on the field numbers of each panel. ... no units on the E field values on panels b and d
concerns.summary: Field values in Fig. 3d-e and Fig. 4b,d lack units.

concerns.quote: The authors repeatedly reference the critical field of switching the moire symmetry Ec but never state that value or indicate it on any of their plots.
concerns.summary: The critical field Ec is referenced repeatedly but its value is not stated.

concerns.quote: I would suggest changing this term by “layer polarization”, which is more commonly used in the literature
concerns.summary: "Superlattice symmetry transition" is confusing because finite displacement field already breaks the symmetry; use "layer polarization".

concerns.quote: In SI 1 page 2, I believe there is an errata: I think it should be t1 ~ sqrt(t2 U) instead of t2 ~ sqrt(t1 U).
concerns.summary: A scaling relation in Supplementary section 1 has its hopping parameters swapped.

concerns.quote: I would suggest defining the interactions Ua, Ub beforehand. It would also be great if the authors could also explicitly say that \Delta ~ U.
concerns.summary: Supplementary section 1 should define Ua and Ub and state the regime Delta ~ U.

later_concerns.quote: the absence of geometric frustration in the honeycomb lattice applies to the possibility of a collinear AFM, but the 120 AFM is frustrated. ... I would suggest to be more honest
later_concerns.summary: The frustration argument only supports a collinear AFM; the text and ED Fig. 12 should admit the AFM spin configuration is not settled.

later_concerns.quote: the abstract says that both the AFM-FM ... and the FM-paramagnet electric-field tuned transitions are new in moire systems. I would suggest highlighting that only the former is new.
later_concerns.summary: Only the electric-field AFM-FM transition is new; the FM to paramagnet transition was shown before.

first_round.quote: There are a few major aspects the authors can improve before further consideration of this manuscript.
I recommend that the manuscript be accepted after major revisions of the written text to improve clarity.

I believe this manuscript presents extensive novel experiments that will be of great interest to the community, I have some issues regarding the clarity of the arguments and calculations that I feel should be addressed before publication

recommendations.note: The file does not indicate a transfer from another journal. The first round (Version 0) has reports from Reviewers 1–3. R1's request rests on 'major aspects' to fix before 'further consideration', plus a requested experiment and analysis separating electric-field and doping effects, so it is inferred as major revision. R3 supports publication but asks mostly for clarifications, comments and corrections, with no new data required, so it is inferred as minor revision; this is a judgement call given the number of points raised. Reviewer 4 appears only in the second round (Version 1), with no first-round report, so is not listed. R1 did not submit a second-round report.
recommendations.label: contested
